text.p: The following are the leading stories in the local press on Friday, July 18. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Bakili Muluzi, opening Malawi's second government controlled radio FM stereo, urged staff at the broadcasting house to be open and accommodate stories from the opposition which has in the past accused him of monopolising the national station.
- Police in Mzuzu, northern Malawi on Wednesday arrested a fellow officer on suspicion that he allowed a Zambian national suspect to escape from prison.

- Government has waived duty on a 120 million kwacha ($7.74 million) 60-bed private hospital construction in Blantyre that will help the country save up to one million kwacha ($67,000) annually in foreign exchange for sending patients abroad, chair for the board of directors, Patrick Makina said on Thursday.

- The introduction of a second radio channel failed its first test on Thursday after listeners were forced to listen to the live coverage of President Bakili Muluzi's opening ceremony on both channels.
- The ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) party heavyweights and Southern Malawi police on Thursday barred the private press access to witness president Bakili Muluzi inaugurating channel 2.

- The ruling party's Southern Malawi governor post which may fall vacant if the incumbent holder Luke Jumbe is dismissed, will pit three cadres as candidates including Works and Supplies minister Abdul Pillane, a southern region committee source said on Thursday.
